Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like early 2019, most likely January 2019. The fed funds rate at 2.40% fits the period after the December 2018 hike. Unemployment of 3.9% also fits.

The market returns support this. US large-cap equity was up 8% over the month, a rebound after the December 2018 selloff. The 6-month return of -3.1% and the 12-month return of -2.4% are consistent with that. Emerging-market equity was up 10.3% in the month, which is also plausible for January 2019.

Other figures fit as well. Payrolls averaged 254k over 3 months, which matches December 2018's strong 312k. The 10-year yield of 2.70% and the 2-year yield of 2.52% are consistent with January 2019. The dollar was up 7.35% year over year, and the Baa spread of 2.37 is consistent with widening in late 2018. Headline CPI at 1.95% fits December 2018 data.

I also considered whether the snapshot could be January 2019 or February 2019. In February, large-cap equity would have been up about 11% over 3 months, which does not match the +2.9% shown. January is the better fit.
